documents.title: 인공지능 및 데이터 기반 행정 활성화에 관한 법률
documents.issuing_body: 행정안전부 (Ministry of the Interior and Safety)
documents.implementation_notes: This law governs AI and data-based administration in the public sector in South Korea. It was originally enacted in 2020 as the 'Data-Based Administration Promotion Act' and significantly amended in February 2026 to incorporate AI governance provisions. Key additions in 2026 include: mandatory pre-deployment AI impact assessment on fundamental rights (Article 32, effective 2027-02-28), AI ethics guidelines for public institutions (Article 31), AI service registry (Article 30), and requirement for public institutions already using AI to conduct impact assessments within 2 years of the amendment's effective date. The document primarily addresses public sector AI use rather than general AI regulation.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The law is primarily framed around enabling and activating AI and data-based public administration to achieve efficient, objective, and scientific governance. The stated purpose is to promote AI/data utilization in public institutions to improve quality of life and institutional accountability. Safety and rights considerations (bias, transparency, privacy, fundamental rights impact assessment) are secondary guardrails attached to the activation agenda rather than the primary drivers.

documents.title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법
documents.implementation_notes: The Act was published 2025-01-21 and takes effect one year after promulgation (approx. 2026-01-22), with a separate effective date of 2026-01-24 for digital medical device provisions. The National AI Strategy Committee under the President expires after 5 years. High-impact AI and large compute-threshold AI carry the most concrete mandatory obligations; third-party certification for high-impact AI is strongly encouraged but not strictly mandatory for private operators (Article 30(3) uses 'shall endeavor'). Extraterritorial scope applies where domestic market or users are affected. National security AI is excluded.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The law's stated purpose explicitly pairs protection of citizens' rights with strengthening national competitiveness ('국가경쟁력을 강화'). The bulk of the legislation establishes industrial promotion frameworks—R&D support, startup activation, AI cluster zones, workforce development, international market access, and investment—making economic competitiveness the dominant frame. Consumer/public safety and fundamental rights protection are substantive secondary frames, addressed through high-impact AI obligations, transparency requirements, and safety research. Innovation enablement is also a strong secondary frame given the extensive support mechanisms for the AI industry.

documents.title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법 시행령
documents.implementation_notes: This is the Enforcement Decree (시행령) implementing the AI Basic Act (인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법). It entered into force 2026-01-22. Key provisions define: (1) compute threshold for frontier AI safety obligations (10^26 FLOPs); (2) high-impact AI (고영향 인공지능) determination procedures; (3) transparency/disclosure obligations for high-impact and generative AI; (4) impact assessment requirements; (5) domestic representative designation thresholds for foreign operators. Defense and national intelligence AI uses are explicitly excluded from coverage (제2조). Civil penalties (과태료) apply per 별표 2, details not reproduced in main text.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The decree primarily frames AI governance around protecting users and the public from harms caused by high-impact AI systems, requiring transparency disclosures, safety obligations, impact assessments focused on life/safety/fundamental rights, and trust-building measures. Fundamental rights protection is a strong secondary frame given explicit references to impacts on 기본권 (basic rights). Innovation enablement and economic competitiveness are also significant secondary frames given extensive provisions for industry promotion, data infrastructure, cluster zones, and international market support.

documents.title: 인공지능 기본법 시행령 제정안 입법예고
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Science and ICT (과학기술정보통신부), Republic of Korea
documents.implementation_notes: This is an enforcement decree (시행령) draft for the AI Basic Act (법률 제20676호, enacted 2025-01-21, effective 2026-01-22). Key provisions: (1) AI systems with cumulative training compute ≥10^26 FLOPs are subject to safety assurance obligations; (2) Transparency obligations apply to AI business operators but are exempted for internal business use; (3) High-impact AI operators must document risk management measures and publish key contents publicly; (4) High-impact AI impact assessments must include use behavior analysis and fundamental rights identification; (5) National security and defense AI applications are explicitly excluded from the Act's scope. Legislative notice period: 2025-11-12 to 2025-12-22.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's stated purpose is to support the healthy development of AI and establish a trust foundation for AI society, explicitly linking this to protecting citizens' rights and dignity, improving quality of life, and strengthening national competitiveness. The bulk of the decree establishes infrastructure for AI development: R&D support, data systems, AI industrial clusters, safety research institutes, and international cooperation. While rights protection and safety obligations (high-impact AI, transparency) are significant secondary concerns, the overall framing prioritizes enabling AI innovation and industry growth as the primary governance rationale.

documents.title: 인공지능 영향평가 가이드라인
documents.issuing_body: 한국지능정보사회진흥원 (National Information Society Agency, NIA) / 과학기술정보통신부 (Ministry of Science and ICT)
documents.implementation_notes: The guideline implements Article 35 of the AI Basic Act (인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법). The impact assessment is framed as a best-effort obligation ('노력하여야 한다') for AI business operators providing high-impact AI products/services, not a strict legal mandate. Public institutions must preferentially consider products/services that have undergone impact assessment. Voluntary self-assessment is encouraged for all AI products. Interoperability with EU FRIA (AI Act Art. 27) and UNESCO Ethical Impact Assessment frameworks is an explicit design goal. Detailed procedures are to be specified by Presidential Decree.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's primary stated purpose is to assess AI impacts on 'basic rights' (기본권) of individuals affected by high-impact AI. The law it implements (Article 35) explicitly frames the assessment as evaluating effects on fundamental rights, human dignity, and inviolable rights. Secondary economic competitiveness framing appears in references to global interoperability, market access, and minimizing regulatory barriers for Korean firms overseas.

documents.title: 인공지능(AI) 프라이버시 리스크 관리 모델
documents.issuing_body: Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC), Republic of Korea
documents.implementation_notes: The model is non-binding guidance ('참고') developed through the AI Privacy Public-Private Policy Council. It covers the full AI lifecycle including pre-training, fine-tuning, and deployment. Future sector-specific guidance for small organizations and startups is planned. The document explicitly states entities may apply it according to their individual circumstances, and it will be updated as law, regulation, and technology evolve.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is centered on protecting individual privacy rights in the context of AI data processing. It frames AI governance as necessary to manage risks to personal information, citing harms like unlawful data collection, profiling, surveillance, and identity inference. The core justification is protecting data subjects' rights under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act, making fundamental_rights the dominant frame. Consumer/public safety is secondary as the document also addresses practical harms from AI outputs.

documents.title: 인공지능 안전성 확보 가이드라인(안)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a draft guideline (안) issued under Article 32 of the AI Basic Act and Article 24 of its Enforcement Decree, and the associated ministerial notice (고시 제2026-○○호). It is explicitly non-binding and does not replace or create new obligations beyond the underlying law. The document may change before final publication. It covers applicability determination, lifecycle risk management (identification, assessment, mitigation), safety incident monitoring, and reporting obligations. The compute threshold for coverage is referenced as 10^25 FLOPs. Government supervision and inspection may reference this guideline.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around ensuring safety of AI systems to protect users and affected persons from harm—covering lifecycle risk management, incident monitoring, and safety measures. The repeated focus on protecting 'life, physical safety, and fundamental rights' of users and affected persons places consumer/public safety as the dominant frame, with fundamental rights as a strong secondary concern.

documents.title: 인공지능 투명성 확보 가이드라인
documents.issuing_body: National Intelligence Agency (NIA) / Ministry of Science and ICT (과학기술정보통신부)
documents.implementation_notes: This guideline operationalizes Article 31 of Korea's AI Basic Act (인공지능 기본법), which imposes three transparency obligations: (1) prior notification that a product/service is operated by high-impact AI or generative AI; (2) labeling that AI-generated outputs were produced by generative AI; (3) labeling of deepfake outputs. The guideline clarifies that transparency obligations fall on the entity directly providing AI products/services to end-users, not upstream model developers unless they directly serve end-users. Foreign operators affecting Korean citizens are also covered. Detailed labeling methods are provided for text, image, video, audio, and other file formats, including both human-perceptible and machine-readable approaches. Artistic/creative works are afforded flexibility in labeling methods.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily around preventing social harms such as confusion, misinformation, deepfake abuse, digital sex crimes, and erosion of public trust. The stated purpose of transparency obligations is to prevent 'confusion and misrepresentation in information use and to enhance social trust.' Risk cases emphasize fake news affecting elections and markets, sexual exploitation, and academic fraud—all social stability concerns. Fundamental rights (especially protection from deepfake sexual abuse) and consumer/public safety are strong secondary frames.

documents.title: 생성형 인공지능 의료기기 허가·심사 가이드라인
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Medical Device Review Division
documents.implementation_notes: This guideline is explicitly non-binding ('not legally effective externally') and serves as guidance for applicants seeking approval for generative AI medical devices under the Digital Medical Products Act. It covers foundation models used within medical applications, excluding general-purpose foundation models not embedded in specific medical applications. Key focus areas include hallucination risk, inconsistency, data quality, and bias management. Post-market real-world evidence collection is recommended but not mandated.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is a South Korean regulatory guideline for approving generative AI medical devices. Its central concern is ensuring patient safety and clinical validity of AI-generated outputs, including risks of hallucination, inconsistency, bias, and data quality failures. The governance rationale is framed primarily around protecting patients from unsafe medical AI outputs, requiring risk management processes, analytical performance validation, and clinical efficacy confirmation. Secondary framing around innovation enablement is present as the guideline aims to provide a workable approval pathway for novel GenAI medical devices. Fundamental rights appear as a minor frame through references to personal data protection.

documents.title: 생성형 인공지능(AI) 개발·활용을 위한 개인정보 처리 안내서(2025.8.)
documents.implementation_notes: This guidance was issued by the Korean Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) in August 2025 specifically for generative AI lifecycle personal data processing. It is regulatory guidance rather than binding law, but references mandatory provisions of the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). Public sector entities face mandatory PIA requirements; private sector compliance is strongly recommended but voluntary for some measures. The document covers the full AI lifecycle (purpose setting, strategy, training/development, deployment/management, governance) and distinguishes obligations between model developers and model users. It references sandbox and pre-review mechanisms that can substitute for certain consent requirements under enhanced safety conditions. Enforcement actions cited include corrective orders, fines, and supervisory investigations by PIPC. Review cycle is every 3 years from August 2025.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is issued by South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission and is explicitly grounded in personal data protection law, framing the governance of generative AI primarily as a matter of protecting individual rights (자유와 권리 보호, 존엄과 가치 구현). The stated purpose is to ensure lawful personal data processing, protect data subjects' rights (access, correction, deletion, objection to automated decisions), and reduce legal uncertainty—all anchored in fundamental rights principles. Secondary framings include consumer/public safety (technical safeguards, red-teaming, AUP) and innovation enablement (regulatory sandbox, pre-compliance reviews to support AI development).

documents.title: 고영향 인공지능 사업자 책무 가이드라인
documents.issuing_body: 과학기술정보통신부 (Ministry of Science and ICT, Republic of Korea) / 한국지능정보사회진흥원 (NIA)
documents.implementation_notes: The guideline explicitly states it has no legal binding force ('가이드라인 자체는 법적 구속력은 없으나 법상 의무 이행을 지원하기 위한 목적으로 제작') but supports compliance with the legally binding obligations of Article 34 of the AI Basic Act (인공지능 기본법). Obligations under Article 34 include: (1) risk management plan establishment and operation; (2) explainability plan for AI outputs, key criteria, and training data; (3) user protection plan; (4) human oversight of high-impact AI; (5) documentation and retention of safety/reliability measures. High-impact AI domains are enumerated in the AI Basic Act and include energy supply, water treatment, healthcare, medical devices, nuclear facility management, biometric data for criminal investigation, hiring and loan review, transportation, public services decision-making, and student assessment in early/primary/secondary education.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's stated rationale centers on protecting citizens' safety and fundamental rights (기본권) from high-impact AI systems. The background section explicitly states the law aims to provide 'legal basis for protecting citizens' safety and fundamental rights alongside AI development.' Operator obligations are framed around human oversight, explainability, user protection, and risk management—all justified by the potential for high-impact AI to significantly affect life, physical safety, and fundamental rights.

documents.title: 인공지능(AI) 개발·서비스를 위한 공개된 개인정보 처리 안내서
documents.implementation_notes: The document explicitly states it has no legal binding force ('법적 구속력이 없음') and presents legal interpretation standards as reference guidance. It applies to overseas AI actors targeting Korean data subjects. The guide covers the full AI lifecycle (training and service stages) and is subject to periodic revision as AI law, technology, and market conditions evolve. The PIPC plans to conduct periodic pre-emptive inspections and prior adequacy reviews, and to revise the Personal Information Protection Act to align with the AI era.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around protecting the fundamental right of informational self-determination (개인정보자기결정권) of data subjects whose publicly available personal information is used in AI training. The governance rationale centers on ensuring data subjects retain rights to access, correction, deletion, and processing suspension even when their data is publicly scraped. Secondary framings include consumer/public safety (preventing leakage and exposure of personal data through AI outputs) and innovation enablement (providing legal clarity to allow AI development within privacy law).

documents.title: 개인정보 영향평가 인공지능 분야 평가항목(안)
documents.issuing_body: Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC), South Korea
documents.implementation_notes: This document is a draft (안) checklist of AI-specific evaluation items for Privacy Impact Assessments (PIA) under South Korean personal information protection law. Items cover: lawful basis for collecting personal data for AI training; safeguards for publicly collected data; third-party transfer and entrustment requirements; cross-border transfer requirements; retention and destruction of training data; security measures against AI vulnerability attacks; role/responsibility definition across the AI supply chain; transparency via privacy policies; acceptable use policy publication for generative AI; and data subject rights mechanisms including deletion of AI-generated facial/voice outputs.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is a privacy impact assessment checklist for AI systems under South Korean data protection law. Its governance rationale centers on protecting individual data subjects' rights—consent, lawful basis, data minimization, deletion, and the right to remove AI-generated outputs of one's face or voice. This is quintessentially a fundamental-rights framing. Secondary consumer/public safety concerns appear in items addressing AI vulnerability attacks and inappropriate AI outputs.

documents.title: 공공기관 인공지능 활용 시 개인정보 보호 강화된다
documents.implementation_notes: This regulatory guidance amends the 'Notification on Personal Information Impact Assessment' to add AI-specific evaluation domains for public sector entities. The assessment criteria are mandatory for public sector organizations above specified thresholds, but the document notes the criteria can also serve as voluntary reference for private sector entities. The two new evaluation domains cover AI system training/development and AI system operation/management. No explicit civil or criminal penalties are mentioned in this press release; enforcement is primarily through mandatory impact assessment obligations.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document centers on protecting personal information rights of data subjects when public institutions deploy AI. The governance justification is framed around preventing privacy violations, ensuring legal bases for data processing, and protecting sensitive groups such as children—core fundamental rights concerns under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act.

documents.title: 공공부문 초거대 AI 도입‧활용 가이드라인
documents.issuing_body: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
documents.implementation_notes: This is a non-binding guideline for public sector adoption of hyperscale AI (초거대 AI / LLM). It provides procedural guidance on data security classification, cloud service configuration, learning methods, service introduction approaches, SLO, and maintenance. It references CSAP certification requirements under the Cloud Computing Act. No explicit prohibited practices or penalties are stated. Publication date is estimated as March 2024 based on internal references to market data as of March 2024.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around enabling public sector adoption of hyperscale AI to improve government service quality, administrative efficiency, and digital platform government goals. The stated purpose is to guide public agencies in introducing AI to streamline work, enhance citizen services, and foster AI innovation ecosystems. Safety and security considerations (data security grades, cloud security certification) appear as prerequisites for adoption rather than the primary justification. Economic competitiveness is secondary, evidenced by references to strengthening Korea's hyperscale AI competitiveness. Consumer/public safety appears as a guardrail concern.

documents.title: 공공부문 초거대 AI 도입·활용 가이드라인 2.0
documents.implementation_notes: This is a non-binding regulatory guidance document (version 2.0, revised April 2025) issued jointly by the Digital Platform Government Committee and NIA for the South Korean public sector. It covers hyperscale/generative AI (초거대 AI/LLM) adoption across central ministries, local governments, and public institutions. Key obligations are framed as principles and checklists rather than legally enforceable mandates. Data security classification (C/S/O) and CSAP cloud certification requirements reference existing binding law (클라우드컴퓨팅법, 정보공개법, N2SF). AI ethics compliance references the MSIT AI Ethics Guidelines (2020). The document does not specify civil or criminal penalties; enforcement relies on existing procurement and cloud security regulatory frameworks. Performance management framework (Part 4) provides KPI pools for AI project lifecycle evaluation.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around enabling public sector adoption of hyperscale AI to modernize government services, improve administrative efficiency, and solve social problems. The dominant rationale throughout is operational enablement: providing procedures, frameworks, and guidelines to help public agencies successfully introduce and use AI technology. Safety and rights protections (data security, AI ethics, personal information) appear as secondary compliance requirements within an overarching innovation-enablement narrative, not as the primary driver. National security concerns appear narrowly in data classification and network security contexts.
